claims.claim: Google multilingual BERT cased checkpoint covers 104 languages and uses BERT-Base shape.
claims.verification_note: Official repository README for the original checkpoint.

claims.claim: Original mBERT uses exponentially smoothed multilingual Wikipedia sampling with S=0.7.
claims.verification_note: Formula is a mathematical restatement; 100:1 example is illustrative.

claims.claim: XLM-R is trained on filtered CommonCrawl across 100 languages and more than two terabytes of text.
claims.verification_note: Source says text bytes, not trillions of tokenizer tokens.

claims.claim: XLM-R paper reports gains of 14.6 average accuracy on XNLI, 13 average F1 on MLQA and 2.4 F1 on NER compared with mBERT.
claims.verification_note: Reported gains belong to paper comparison under its stated evaluation.

claims.claim: XNLI is a cross-lingual NLI benchmark with translated evaluation datasets.
claims.verification_note: Zero-shot versus translated evaluation protocols must be distinguished.

claims.claim: Official XLM-R Base checkpoint uses its own SentencePiece tokenizer and should not share token IDs with a BERT checkpoint.
